item.title: Race- and Neighborhood-Level Social Determinants of Health in Diagnosis and Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation
item.dc:creator: Kano Amagai
Alya Nadji
Melissa Berkowitz
Atheendar S. Venkataramani
Erica L. Dixon
item.description:
Authors: Kano Amagai, Alya Nadji, Melissa Berkowitz, Atheendar S. Venkataramani, Erica L. Dixon
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2640279
Abstract: Importance Early diagnosis and treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF) is critical for preventing stroke, heart failure, and mortality. Understanding patterns in diagnosis and treatment of AF may improve detection and reduce disparities. Objective To evaluate the interactions between race and ethnicity and neighborhood social determinants of health on AF diagnosis and treatment. Design, Setting, and Participants Retrospective cohort study using administrative claims for greater Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, area residents aged 18 years or older from Independence Blue Cross from 2017 to 2021. Baseline characteristics were assessed in 2017, and participants were followed up from 2018 through 2021. Data were analyzed from October 2023 to July 2026. Exposures Exposures included Non-Hispanic Black race and ethnicity, neighborhood-level social determinants of health as measured by the social barrier index (SBI), and the interaction between the two. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was AF diagnosis ascertained from International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision diagnosis codes. The secondary outcome was anticoagulant prescription among individuals with AF diagnoses as ascertained from pharmacy claims. Results Of the 504 876 patients included, the mean (SD) age was 48 (18) years; 267 596 (53.0%) were female; 67 362 (13.3%) non-Hispanic Black, and 437 514 (86.7%) were non-Hispanic White. A total of 27 249 patients (5.1%) were diagnosed with AF during the study period. Non-Hispanic Black patients were less likely to be diagnosed with AF compared with non-Hispanic White patients (odds ratio [OR], 0.91; 95% CI, 0.82-1.00). The relative difference increased with increased SBI (which denotes more vulnerable neighborhoods) as shown by a significant interaction between race and ethnicity and SBI (OR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.86-0.95). Among those diagnosed with AF, 15 722 (58%) had an anticoagulant prescription. There was a significant interaction between race and ethnicity and SBI (OR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.00-1.20), suggesting that filled prescription patterns differed by race and ethnicity with SBI. For Black individuals one unit increase in SBI was associated with decreased odds of AF diagnosis (OR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.90-0.99). For White individuals one unit increase in SBI was associated with increased odds of AF diagnosis (OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.03-1.07). Conclusions and Relevance This cohort study of Medicare Advantage and commercially insured individuals found that AF diagnosis rates declined with worsening neighborhood-level disadvantage among non-Hispanic Black individuals but increased among non-Hispanic White individuals. Conditional on diagnoses, rates of prescription of anticoagulants were similar across race and ethnicity groups. Targeted interventions, especially in more marginalized neighborhoods, are needed to increase detection of AF.

item.title: Weight Gain During Pregnancy and Severe Maternal Morbidity
item.dc:creator: Sahar Khademioore
Elizabeth K. Darling
Rohan D’Souza
Giulia M. Muraca
Yanfang Guo
Laura N. Anderson
item.description:
Authors: Sahar Khademioore, Elizabeth K. Darling, Rohan D’Souza, Giulia M. Muraca, Yanfang Guo, Laura N. Anderson
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2640027
Abstract: Importance Severe maternal morbidity (SMM) carries serious consequences for pregnant individuals, yet the association between gestational weight gain (GWG) and SMM remains poorly understood. Objective To examine the association between GWG and SMM across prepregnancy body mass index (BMI) categories. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cohort study used linked birth registry data from Better Outcomes Registry &amp;amp; Network Ontario and hospitalization data from the Canadian Institute for Health Information for singleton pregnancies with a hospital delivery at a gestational age of 20 weeks or greater in Ontario, Canada, from April 1, 2012, to March 31, 2022. Data were analyzed from May 1 to November 1, 2025. Exposures Continuous GWG as mean weekly gain in the second and third trimesters and categorical GWG (inadequate, adequate, or excessive) according to the 2009 Institute of Medicine recommendations based on prepregnancy BMI. Main Outcomes and Measures SMM, defined as a composite of 13 indicators per the Canadian Perinatal Surveillance System, occurring during delivery hospitalization. Results Among 1 035 927 pregnancies, 192 731 (18.6%) had inadequate, 296 448 (28.6%) had adequate, and 546 748 (52.8%) had excessive GWG; 15 119 (14.59 per 1000 births) experienced SMM. Compared with adequate GWG, excessive GWG was associated with increased SMM across all BMI categories: underweight (adjusted rate ratio [ARR], 1.33 [95% CI, 1.15-1.53]), normal weight (ARR, 1.24 [95% CI, 1.17-1.31]), overweight (ARR, 1.16 [95% CI, 1.06-1.27]), obesity class I (ARR, 1.21 [95% CI, 1.08-1.35]), obesity class II (ARR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.07-1.54]), and obesity class III (ARR, 1.24 [95% CI, 1.03-1.48]). Inadequate GWG was associated with increased SMM predominantly among individuals with normal weight (ARR, 1.13 [95% CI, 1.06-1.21]) and overweight (ARR, 1.19 [95% CI, 1.05-1.35]). GWG showed nonlinear associations with SMM across all BMI categories, with risk elevated at both low and high GWG in individuals with underweight, normal weight, and overweight, while in those with obesity classes I to III, risk was concentrated at high GWG values. Estimated SMM rates were lowest at 0.4 kg/wk GWG for underweight through overweight BMI categories and declined across obesity classes to 0.1 kg/wk GWG for the obesity class III category. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of 1 035 927 pregnancies, GWG outside Institute of Medicine–recommended ranges was associated with increased SMM risk, with patterns varying by BMI category. These findings may complement existing evidence informing GWG guidance.

item.title: Quantitative Flow Ratio– vs Angiography-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention
item.dc:creator: Han Zhang
Yanpu Shi
Changdong Guan
Jingang Cui
Xiaofan Wu
Lianglong Chen
Chengxing Shen
Junqing Yang
item.description:
Authors: Han Zhang, Yanpu Shi, Changdong Guan, Jingang Cui, Xiaofan Wu, Lianglong Chen, Chengxing Shen, Junqing Yang, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639926
Abstract: Importance Whether the association of quantitative flow ratio (QFR)–guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with long-term outcomes differs according to multivessel disease (MVD) status is uncertain. Objective To assess the association of QFR-guided vs angiography-guided PCI with 3-year outcomes according to MVD status. Design, Setting, and Participants In this prespecified secondary analysis of the FAVOR III China randomized clinical trial, patients were screened across 26 centers in China from December 25, 2018, to January 19, 2020. Eligible participants were adults undergoing PCI for stable or unstable angina or for myocardial infarction (MI) occurring at least 72 hours before screening who had at least 1 lesion with 50% to 90% diameter stenosis in a vessel of 2.5 mm or larger. The analysis compared QFR-guided with angiography-guided PCI according to MVD status. MVD was defined by involvement of at least 2 epicardial vessels or the left main coronary artery. The primary analyses of the current prespecified secondary analysis were completed in October 2024. Interventions Randomization 1:1 to QFR-guided PCI or angiography-guided PCI. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary end point of the FAVOR III China randomized clinical trial was 1-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as a composite of all-cause death, MI, and ischemia-driven revascularization. The current analysis evaluated 3-year MACE. Results Among 3825 patients in the intention-to-treat population (mean [SD] age, 62.7 [10.0] years; 2699 [70.6%] male), 2066 (54.0%) had MVD. In the MVD cohort, MACE occurred in 124 of 1023 patients (12.1%) in the QFR-guided group and 188 of 1043 patients (18.1%) in the angiography-guided group (hazard ratio, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.52-0.81; P &amp;lt; .001), driven by lower rates of MI and revascularization. In the non-MVD cohort, MACE occurred in 76 of 890 patients (8.6%) and 95 of 869 patients (11.0%), respectively (hazard ratio, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.57-1.04; P = .09). The treatment × MVD interaction was not statistically significant ( P for interaction = .35). The findings of landmark, per-protocol, competing-risk, sensitivity, and hierarchical win-ratio analyses were directionally consistent with the main findings. Conclusions and Relevance In this prespecified secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial of patients undergoing PCI, QFR-guided PCI was associated with a lower 3-year MACE rate among patients with MVD; however, no significant interaction was observed between treatment effect and MVD status. These findings provide longer-term randomized evidence supporting QFR-guided PCI across MVD strata and warrant further confirmation. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03656848

Authors: Anna E. Fiastro, Erin K. Thayer, Samantha N. Fredman, Mary Stoa, Sara Manns, Sarah B. Munro, Emmalie Griswold, Abigail Aiken, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2640034
Abstract: Importance In states that restrict abortion provision, residents rely on telehealth medication abortion (teleMAB) or travel out of state for in-clinic care; however, little is known about how patients using these modalities differ. Objective To compare characteristics of Kansas and Texas residents receiving teleMAB vs in-clinic medication abortion and to assess geographic and socioeconomic factors associated with modality of care. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cross-sectional analysis used electronic medical record data for patients residing in Kansas or Texas who received medication abortion care from a teleMAB service or from an abortion facility in Kansas from February 1 to June 30, 2024. Patients younger than 18 years were excluded because only the telehealth site served this age group. Exposure Patient sociodemographic characteristics (age, race and ethnicity, and number of children), gestational age, and county-level distance to the nearest abortion facility, social vulnerability, and rural-urban designation. Main Outcomes and Measures The main outcome was receipt of teleMAB vs in-clinic care. Differences between patients who received teleMAB vs in-clinic care were assessed using χ 2 and t tests for bivariate variables and multivariable logistic regression for adjusted comparisons. Results The teleMAB service served 12 823 patients (Texas: n = 12 552; Kansas: n = 271); the clinic served 725 patients (Texas: n = 587; Kansas: n = 138). Mean (SD) age was 26 (6) years for Kansas residents and 27 (6) years for Texas residents. In both states, more telehealth patients self-identified as Hispanic, Latino, Latina, or Latine (Texas: 3739 of 12 552 [32%]; Kansas: 48 of 271 [18%]) than in-clinic patients (Texas: 14 of 587 [3%]; Kansas: 8 of 138 [7%]) ( P &amp;lt; .001). This difference remained among Texas residents after adjustment. In both states, compared with in-clinic patients, telehealth patients were more likely to be at less than 6 weeks’ gestation (Texas: 7648 of 12 552 [61%] vs 155 of 587 [27%]; Kansas: 159 of 271 [59%] vs 45 of 138 [33%]; P &amp;lt; .001) and to have no children (Texas: 5545 of 12 552 [44%] vs 42 of 587 [7%]; Kansas: 137 of 271 [51%] vs 5 of 138 [4%]; P &amp;lt; .001). In Texas, patients who lived farthest from in-clinic care were more likely to receive telehealth than those who lived shorter distances (average marginal effect, 0.003; 95% CI, 0.002-0.004). Conclusions and Relevance In this cross-sectional study of patients who used medication abortion, teleMAB patients more often had no children, were living farther from an abortion facility, and represented populations facing structural racism and long-documented barriers to abortion care compared with in-clinic patients, particularly in abortion-restrictive states. A higher number of patients at lower gestational age received telehealth than in-clinic services, suggesting more convenient and timely care.

item.description:
Authors: Sang Heon Suh, Hong Sang Choi, Chang Seong Kim, Eun Hui Bae, Jayoun Kim, Ji Yong Jung, Jong Cheol Jeong, Kyu-Beck Lee, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2634568
Abstract: Importance While protein restriction is a cornerstone of chronic kidney disease (CKD) management, its long-term benefits on clinical outcomes in Asian populations, who often have lower body mass and muscle reserves, remain unclear. Objective To investigate the association between daily protein intake (DPI) and the risk of kidney failure requiring replacement therapy (KFRT) and all-cause mortality in patients with non–dialysis-dependent CKD. Design, Setting, and Participants This prospective cohort study used data from the Korean Cohort Study for Outcomes in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease (KNOW-CKD). Participants with CKD at stages ranging from 1 to predialysis 5 were enrolled between 2011 and 2016 from 9 tertiary hospitals in South Korea. The study observation period ended on January 31, 2024. Data analysis was performed from February 2024 to May 2026. Exposures DPI was objectively estimated using 24-hour urinary nitrogen excretion at baseline. The participants were categorized by DPI: less than 0.6, 0.6 to less than 0.8, 0.8 to less than 1.0, 1.0 to less than 1.2, and 1.2 or greater. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was the onset of KFRT. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models were used to account for the competing risk of death. Results A total of 1861 participants (mean [SD] age, 53.7 [12.0] years; 1304 [61.1%] male) were analyzed, with a median (range) follow-up of 9.3 (0.01-12.37) years. The lowest DPI group (&amp;lt;0.6 g/kg/d) was associated with increased risk of KFRT (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 1.42; 95% CI, 1.09-1.85) as well as all-cause mortality (sHR, 2.17; 95% CI, 1.17-4.03), but not MACEs, compared with the highest DPI group (&amp;gt;1.2 g/kg/d). Furthermore, a nonlinear association was observed, where excessively low protein intake was associated with an increased risk of KFRT. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of 1861 patients with nondialysis CKD, low protein intake was not associated with significant nephroprotection and was associated with a higher risk of KFRT and all-cause mortality. These findings suggest that rigid protein restriction should be balanced with nutritional monitoring to prevent protein-energy wasting, particularly in populations with lower muscle mass, and a more individualized approach to dietary protein management in CKD may be warranted.

item.title: Emotion-Focused Behavioral Weight Loss Treatment for Adolescents
item.dc:creator: Kerri N. Boutelle
Michael A. Manzano
Ellen K. Pasquale
David R. Strong
Rebecca S. Bernard
Kyung E. Rhee
Dawn M. Eichen

item.description:
Authors: Kerri N. Boutelle, Michael A. Manzano, Ellen K. Pasquale, David R. Strong, Rebecca S. Bernard, Kyung E. Rhee, Dawn M. Eichen, Alec Miller, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639867
Abstract: Importance Family-based behavioral treatment (FBT) efficacy decreases in adolescence, a developmental period of gradual maturation and increasing autonomy during which emotion regulation skills develop. Objective To evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of FBT alone compared with FBT plus emotion regulation across 6 months of treatment and 12 months of follow-up on adolescent weight change, emotion regulation, emotional eating, and parent weight change. Design, Setting, and Participants This parallel-group randomized clinical trial of adolescents 13 to 16 years of age with body mass index (BMI) in the 85th percentile or higher but less than the 99.9th percentile was conducted from August 29, 2019, to January 4, 2024, at 2 university clinics. Central randomization was completed by a statistician, and outcome assessors were blinded to treatment condition. The majority of treatments and assessments were delivered remotely via video conference due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Interventions FBT plus emotion regulation vs traditional FBT skills alone for weight loss. FBT included nutrition and physical activity education, behavior change strategies, and parenting skills. Both treatments had 6 months of adolescent and parent groups and behavior coaching sessions. The combined group included FBT skills and added dialectical behavior therapy and emotion-focused therapy. Main Outcomes and Measures The main outcomes were adolescent weight (body mass index [BMI] z score (BMIz) and BMI as a percentage of the 95th BMI percentile [%BMIp95]), emotion regulation skills (measured by Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale [DERS] scores), emotional eating behaviors (measured by Emotional Eating Scale [EES] scores), parent weight, and feasibility and acceptability of treatment. Primary outcome analyses used an intention-to-treat approach. Results A total of 166 (FBT plus emotion regulation = 84; FBT = 82) dyads (adolescents: mean [SD] age, 14.3 [1.2] years; 95 [57%] female; mean [SD] BMIz, 2.2 [0.6]; mean [SD] %BMIp95, 120.4 [21.4]; parents: mean [SD] age, 45.3 [6.5] years; 141 [85%] female; mean [SD] BMI, 32.6 [7.0]) were assessed at baseline, midtreatment, posttreatment, and 6- and 12-month follow-up visits. There were no statistically significant differences in posttreatment weight loss among adolescents receiving FBT plus emotion regulation compared with FBT (difference in BMIz, 0.03 [95% CI, −0.05 to 0.10]). However, adolescents in FBT plus emotion regulation did not regain as much weight at the 12-month follow-up (difference in BMIz, −0.09 [95% CI, −0.17 to −0.02]). At the 12-month follow-up, 4% (95% CI, 1%-12%) of adolescents in FBT and 22% (95% CI, 8%-48%) of adolescents in FBT plus emotion regulation lost a clinically significant amount of weight (≥0.20 BMIz). At 12 months’ follow-up, parent weight (difference in BMI, 0.51 [95% CI, −0.03 to 1.05]) and adolescent emotion regulation (difference in DERS scores, −0.06 [95% CI, −0.25 to 0.50]) did not differ by treatment. By contrast, the FBT plus emotion regulation group had lower scores than the FBT group on emotional eating (difference in EES scores, −0.39 [95% CI, −0.63 to −0.15]). Conclusions and Relevance In this randomized clinical trial of 166 parent-adolescent dyads, adding emotion regulation skills to FBT did not improve weight loss during treatment but was associated with less weight regain and lower emotional eating through the 12-month follow-up. These findings suggest that adding emotion regulation skills to an FBT program may attenuate weight regain and decrease emotional eating among adolescents. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03674944

item.title: Denosumab Therapy Duration and Osteonecrosis of the Jaw and Skeletal Events in Bone-Metastatic Prostate Cancer
item.dc:creator: Seoree Kim
Seungpil Jung
Seonghyeon Bu
Jin Woo Kim
Sung Woon Pyo
Guk Jin Lee

item.description:
Authors: Seoree Kim, Seungpil Jung, Seonghyeon Bu, Jin Woo Kim, Sung Woon Pyo, Guk Jin Lee, Sang Hoon Chun, In-Ho Kim, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639765
Abstract: Importance Denosumab reduces skeletal-related events in bone-metastatic prostate cancer but carries a cumulative risk of medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ). The treatment duration that best balances these risks has not been established in clinical settings. Objective To evaluate the association between duration of denosumab treatment and the 3-year cumulative incidence of ONJ and skeletal events. Design, Setting, and Participants This nationwide retrospective cohort study emulated a target trial using Korean Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service data from January 1, 2009, through August 31, 2024; patients were not randomized. A clone-censor-weight approach with inverse probability of censoring weighting estimated 3-year cumulative incidence and risk ratios (RRs), with death as a competing event. Men included in the analysis had bone-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and initiated oncologic-dose denosumab therapy; men with castration-sensitive disease were excluded. Exposures Six strategies defined by 3 durations (≤6, 7-12, and ≥13 months), each as a schedule-flexible group and a schedule-adherent subgroup (intervals ≤12 weeks). Main Outcomes and Measures Three-year cumulative incidence of ONJ and skeletal events (pathologic fracture, spinal cord compression, and surgery to bone) was the primary outcome; a radiotherapy-inclusive conventional composite of skeletal-related events was assessed as a secondary outcome. Results Among 3307 men included in the analysis (mean [SD] age, 72.6 [8.6] years; median follow-up, 42.6 [IQR, 26.5-57.4] months), the overall 3-year cumulative incidence was 9.8% (95% CI, 8.7%-11.0%) for ONJ and 4.9% (95% CI, 4.2%-5.7%) for skeletal events. Relative to treatment for 6 months or less, treatment for 7 to 12 months showed a lower risk of skeletal events (3.82% [95% CI, 3.04%-4.80%] vs 5.76% [95% CI, 4.23%-7.79%]; RR, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.45-0.97]) and higher risk of ONJ (3.28% [95% CI, 2.41%-4.44%] vs 1.47% [95% CI, 0.86%-2.50%]; RR, 2.22 [95% CI, 1.21-4.11]). Compared with 7 to 12 months, treatment for 13 months or longer was associated with higher risk of ONJ (12.20% [95% CI, 10.86%-13.68%]; risk difference, 8.93 [95% CI, 7.16-10.64] percentage points), without further reduction in risk for skeletal events (3.99% [95% CI, 3.30%-4.82%]; risk difference, 0.17 [95% CI, −1.03 to 1.31] percentage points). Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of bone-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, denosumab treatment for 7 to 12 months was associated with lower risk of skeletal events and a modest increase in ONJ, whereas treatment beyond 12 months was associated with markedly higher ONJ risk but no further reduction of skeletal events. These findings support individualized reassessment of denosumab treatment duration after approximately 1 year.

item.title: Clinical Outcomes After Recovered, Positive, and Negative Pulse Oximetry Screening Results Among Newborns
item.dc:creator: Lassi Karppi
Panu Kiviranta
Ulla Sankilampi
item.description:
Authors: Lassi Karppi, Panu Kiviranta, Ulla Sankilampi
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639860
Abstract: Importance Pulse oximetry screening (POS) detects critical congenital heart defects (CCHDs) and other neonatal morbidities, but the clinical significance of initially abnormal results that normalize on repeat testing remains unclear. Objective To assess the prevalence and clinical implications of positive, recovered, and negative early POS results in asymptomatic newborns. Design, Setting, and Participants This population-based cohort study included asymptomatic neonates born at 35 weeks’ gestation or later who underwent early POS at 2 to 6 hours of age at a tertiary-level university hospital in Eastern Finland between January 1, 2012, and December 31, 2019. Data were analyzed from August 2025 to August 2026. Exposure Positive POS result or indeterminate POS result that normalized to a negative POS result (recovered) with repeat testing. Main Outcomes and Measures Primary outcomes were neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission and continued hospitalization at 7 days; secondary outcomes included diagnostic investigations and neonatal morbidities. Associations between POS screening results and outcomes were examined using modified Poisson regression adjusted for maternal age, parity, body mass index, and cigarette smoking during pregnancy and newborn sex, gestational age, and birth weight Z score. Results The cohort included 16 599 newborns born at 35 weeks’ gestation or later who underwent early POS at 2 to 6 hours of age (8349 [50.3%] female; mean [SD] gestational age, 39.8 [1.3] weeks). POS results were negative in 16 160 newborns (97.4%), recovered in 208 (1.3%), and positive in 231 (1.4%). Compared with a negative POS result, a recovered or positive POS result was associated with higher risk of NICU admission (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 5.62 [95% CI, 4.58-6.91] and 13.04 [95% CI, 11.77-14.44], respectively) and continued hospitalization at 7 days (ARR, 4.70 [95% CI, 3.07-7.19] and 11.97 [95% CI, 9.26-15.47], respectively). Recovered POS was also associated with greater risk of antibiotic exposure before 72 hours of life (ARR, 5.45 [95% CI, 3.94-7.52]) and need for respiratory support (ARR, 10.16 [3.53-29.21]) compared with a negative result. Respiratory disease was more common in newborns with recovered than negative POS results (27 [13.0%] vs 214 [1.3%]), as were sepsis (10 [4.8%] vs 127 [0.8%]) and hypoglycemia (17 [8.2%] vs 565 [3.5%]). No CCHD occurred among newborns with recovered POS. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of neonates born at 35 weeks’ gestation or later, those with initially indeterminate POS results that normalized on repeat testing had increased risks of treatable neonatal conditions and hospital care but not of CCHD. Further prospective studies should investigate whether targeted assessment of these newborns could reduce morbidity and prolonged hospitalization.

item.description:
Authors: In-Ho Kim, Chang Gon Kim, Jungmin Jo, Eun Hee Jung, Joo-Hwan Park, Woo Kyun Bae, Seok Jae Huh, Yoon Ji Choi, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639846
Abstract: Importance Initial enfortumab vedotin (EV) dose selection is increasingly relevant in advanced urothelial carcinoma (UC). Reduced starting doses may be selected for some patients, but their associations with clinical outcomes and tolerability remain uncertain. Objective To evaluate the association of physician-selected initial EV dose reduction with clinical outcomes among patients with advanced UC. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective multicenter cohort study of patients with advanced UC who initiated EV monotherapy after platinum-based chemotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibition was conducted at 18 institutions in Korea from January 1, 2023, to May 31, 2025, with follow-up through May 31, 2026. Data were analyzed in June 2026. Exposures Initial EV dose reduction at first administration, before treatment-related toxicity. The primary comparison was reduced-dose (≥10% reduction) vs full-dose (&amp;lt;10% reduction) EV monotherapy; post hoc analyses used less than 10%, 10% to 20%, and greater than 20% categories. Main Outcomes and Measures Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were the primary outcomes. Secondary outcomes included objective response and treatment-emergent peripheral neuropathy (PN). Results Among 368 patients (median [IQR] age, 68.0 [62.0-74.0] years; 267 male [72.6%] and 101 female [27.4%]), median (IQR) follow-up was 15.4 (8.4-20.0) months. Median PFS was 5.7 months in the reduced-dose group and 6.3 months in the full-dose group (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.24; 95% CI, 0.95-1.61); median OS was 10.1 and 10.5 months, respectively (adjusted HR, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.81-1.43). Objective response occurred in 65 of 146 response-evaluable patients (44.5%) in the reduced-dose group and 95 of 179 (53.1%) in the full-dose group. Grade 3 or higher PN occurred in 6 of 170 reduced-dose patients (3.5%) and 20 of 198 full-dose patients (10.1%) (adjusted odds ratio, 0.26; 95% CI, 0.09-0.73). In post hoc analyses, reductions exceeding 20% were associated with shorter PFS compared with the full-dose group (adjusted HR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.01-1.95), although the overall 3-group comparison was not statistically significant. Conclusions and Relevance In this multicenter cohort study, physician-selected initial EV dose reduction was not significantly associated with survival or response outcomes. These findings do not establish equivalence or warrant routine initial dose reduction. The lower incidence of severe PN and the exploratory PFS signal with reductions exceeding 20% are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

item.dc:creator: Maria Elena Martinez

Valesca Largaespada

Borsika A. Rabin
Sheila F. Castañeda

item.description:
Authors: Maria Elena Martinez, Scott Roesch, Valesca Largaespada, Jesse N. Nodora, Borsika A. Rabin, Sheila F. Castañeda, Jennifer Covin, Kristine Ortwine, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639013
Abstract: Importance Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening is suboptimal among people in traditionally underserved populations, many of whom receive primary care at federally qualified health centers (FQHCs). Mailed fecal immunochemical test (FIT) outreach improves screening, especially in underserved populations, but questions remain about impact over time. Objective To evaluate the effectiveness of centralized annual mailed FIT outreach delivered over 3 years to increase CRC screening in FQHCs. Design, Setting, and Participants This cluster randomized clinical trial was conducted between June 1, 2021, and May 31, 2024. Sixteen clinics from 2 FQHCs in Southern California were randomly assigned to mailed FIT outreach or usual care for patients aged 50 to 75 years and not up to date with screening. Intervention Intervention components followed best practices for mailed FIT outreach and included educational primers, FIT kits, and telephone reminders. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was the proportion of individuals up to date with any CRC screening after 3 years of intervention (point prevalence); screening at 2 years was a secondary outcome. Due to a resource constraint–related protocol modification, mailed FIT outreach began earlier in year 3, such that some individuals who completed screening in year 2 were not yet due for repeat FIT. Results Among 16 clinics serving 20 250 patients, 6 clinics serving 8334 individuals at baseline (4435 aged 55-64 years [53.2%]; 4896 female [58.7%]; 341 Asian [4.1%], 238 Black [2.9%], 2390 Hispanic [28.7%], and 4371 non-Hispanic White [52.4%]) were randomized to intervention and 10 clinics serving 11 916 individuals at baseline (6443 aged 55-64 years [54.1%]; 7250 female [60.8%]; 699 Asian [5.9%], 355 Black [3.0%], 4635 Hispanic [38.9%], and 4436 non-Hispanic White [37.2%]) were randomized to usual care. At year 3, screening was 39.4% (95% CI, 36.3% to 42.6%) in intervention clinics vs 36.5% (95% CI, 31.2% to 42.2%) in usual care clinics, which was not a statistically significant difference (2.9 percentage points; 95% CI, −3.2 to 9.0 percentage points). At year 2, screening was 37.8% (95% CI, 35.2% to 40.4%) in intervention clinics vs 27.0% (95% CI, 21.8% to 32.9%) in usual care clinics (difference, 10.8 percentage points; 95% CI, 4.9 to 16.7 percentage points). Conclusions and Relevance This study’s findings suggest that centralized mailed FIT outreach could increase CRC screening in FQHCs serving populations with persistent disparities, although maintaining intervention fidelity and providing ongoing implementation support over time are needed for consistent impact. item.dc:creator: James P. Marcin

Authors: James P. Marcin, Jennifer L. Rosenthal, Daniel J. Tancredi, Tanya Rinderknecht, Michelle Y. Hamline, Holly Leshikar, Marike Zwienenberg, Joseph M. Galante, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2636546
Abstract: Importance Telephone consultations for acutely injured children receiving care in emergency departments (EDs) in nonpediatric trauma centers frequently exclude direct communication and informed decision-making with parents. The use of telemedicine to facilitate real-time expert consultation and parental communication with pediatric trauma specialists is underexplored and may improve family experience and support clinical decision-making. Objective To examine the impact of telemedicine on parent experience of care, parent distress, and transfer frequency for acutely injured children presenting to EDs in nonpediatric trauma centers. Design, Setting, and Participants This stepped-wedge cluster-randomized clinical trial recruited patients between November 30, 2020, and November 27, 2022. Participants included families of children younger than 18 years with acute physical trauma presenting to 1 of 10 nonpediatric trauma centers in northern California. Analyses were conducted between June 2023 and March 2026. Interventions EDs were randomized to use telemedicine following a standard telephone consultation or the standard of care (telephone consultation only) when consulting with pediatric trauma physicians. Main Outcomes and Measures Primary outcomes were parent experience of care and parent distress measured 3 days or more following the child's injury. Experience of care was measured using ED Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems (CAHPS) questions. Distress was measured using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory Form Y survey. Modified intention-to-treat analyses were performed to evaluate outcomes. Results The study included 595 children with acute physical trauma with a mean (SD) age of 7.6 (5.1) years, of whom 369 (62.0%) were assigned to telemedicine and 226 (38.0%) to standard of care. Summary scores for parent experience of care 3 days post injury were similar between cohorts (adjusted mean difference [AMD], 0.041 [95% CI, −0.008 to 0.090; P = .10]), as were parent distress summary scores (AMD, −0.031 [95% CI, −0.297 to 0.235; P = .82]). The adjusted odds ratio for transfer of patients assigned to telemedicine was 0.59 (95% CI, 0.16 to 2.16; P = .43). Subscale analyses found significantly higher parental ED discharge and/or transfer experience ratings for patients assigned to telemedicine (AMD, 0.104 [95% CI, 0.023 to 0.186; P = .01]). Conclusions and Relevance In this randomized clinical trial, telemedicine consultations did not differ statistically significantly from standard care with respect to parent experience of care, distress, and transfer rates. Subscale analyses suggested a potential improvement with telemedicine consultations in parent experience related to ED discharge and interfacility transfers, highlighting a potential benefit in communication and preparation during care transitions. item.title: Dual Health and Economic Burden of Multimorbidity in Aging Populations
item.dc:creator: Wenjing Ji
Jiacheng Zheng
Suzhen Guan
Yang Liu
Xi Chen
Zhuoer Lin
Joan Costa-Font
Reshma Aziz Merchant
item.description:
Authors: Wenjing Ji, Jiacheng Zheng, Suzhen Guan, Yang Liu, Xi Chen, Zhuoer Lin, Joan Costa-Font, Reshma Aziz Merchant, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2633002
Abstract: Importance Population aging is contributing to rising multimorbidity across physical, psychological, and cognitive domains, yet global evidence integrating health and economic burdens in older adults remains limited. Objectives To quantify the global health and economic burden of multimorbidity among adults aged 60 years or older and to assess trends from 2000 to 2023. Design, Setting, and Participants This economic evaluation used observational modeling of Global Burden of Disease study 2023 estimates as health inputs and integrated them with macroeconomic, health expenditure, and population data from World Bank Open Data, the World Health Organization Global Health Expenditure Database, and United Nations population data. Health burden analyses covered adults aged 60 years or older in 204 countries and territories from 2000 to 2023, and economic burden analyses covered 180 countries and territories. Data analyses were performed from January 27 to July 22, 2026. Exposures Cross-domain multimorbidity spanning physical conditions, psychological disorders, and cognitive disorders, operationalized as 78 multimorbidity combinations. Main Outcomes and Measures The main outcomes were years lived with disability (YLDs) per 100 000 population and economic losses. All economic indicators are reported in 2021 international dollars (USD) adjusted for purchasing power parity. Joinpoint regression characterized 2000 to 2023 trends. Results From 2000 to 2023, total YLDs increased from 2367.81 (95% uncertainty interval [UI], 1067.67-4969.59) to 2941.68 (95% UI, 1252.99-6816.95) per 100 000 population, while economic losses increased from $80.10 billion (95% UI, $59.60-$104.69 billion) to $363.25 billion (95% UI, $264.04-$502.74 billion). The highest 2023 YLD rate was observed for osteoarthritis and Alzheimer disease and other dementias (369.87 [95% UI, 163.86-752.23] per 100 000 population), whereas the largest 2023 economic loss was observed for osteoarthritis and anxiety disorders ($48.51 billion [95% UI, $31.68-$76.57 billion]). The fastest-growing combination was diabetes, anxiety disorders, and Parkinson disease, with a YLD average annual percentage change (AAPC) of 3.94% (95% CI, 3.79%-4.08%) and an economic loss AAPC of 9.92% (95% CI, 9.69%-10.13%). Conclusions and Relevance In this economic evaluation of the global health and economic burden of multimorbidity among adults aged 60 years or older, multimorbidity burden increased worldwide, with economic losses growing faster than YLDs. Heterogeneity across sex, country income groups, and disease combinations, together with divergence between disability and economic burden, suggest that policy priorities for aging populations should consider both health burden and economic vulnerability.

item.title: Multiple Dimensions of Social Vulnerability and Cervical Cancer Screening Uptake
item.dc:creator: Julie Haury
Jean Baptiste Chanier
Bruno Renevier
Geoffroy Canlorbe
Simon Crequit
item.description:
Authors: Julie Haury, Jean Baptiste Chanier, Bruno Renevier, Geoffroy Canlorbe, Simon Crequit
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639570
Abstract: Importance Despite organized screening programs, persistent social inequalities undermine cervical cancer screening effectiveness in high-income countries, disproportionately affecting the most socially vulnerable women. Objectives To identify distinct social vulnerability profiles among pregnant women and examine their associations with cervical cancer screening adherence and intraepithelial lesion detection. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cohort study assessed all pregnant women 25 years or older who delivered at Centre Hospitalier Intercommunal André-Grégoire, a single tertiary care maternity unit in France, between May 1, 2019, and May 1, 2025. Exposures Social vulnerability was assessed across 15 indicators spanning administrative, psychological, and violence-related domains. Multiple component analysis and hierarchical clustering on principal components identified 6 distinct vulnerability profiles. Multiple logistic regression examined associations between profiles and cervical screening inadequacy (no cervical sample within the last 3 years, including those never screened) and squamous intraepithelial lesion detection, adjusting for maternal age and body mass index. Main Outcomes and Measures Cervical screening inadequacy (primary outcome) and low- and high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion detection (secondary outcome). Results Among 18 253 women (median [IQR] age, 32.3 [29.1-36.0] years; median [IQR] body mass index, 25.9 [22.7-29.4]), 10 248 (56.1%) were up to date with screening. Six vulnerability profiles were identified. Compared with the low-vulnerability reference profile, all profiles showed increased odds of screening inadequacy: substance use and psychological vulnerability (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 1.33; 95% CI, 1.20-1.48), migrant or linguistic barrier (AOR, 3.40; 95% CI, 3.16-3.66), psychological violence (AOR, 2.01; 95% CI, 1.75-2.32), sexual violence (AOR, 2.08; 95% CI, 1.74-2.48), and physical violence (AOR, 2.54; 95% CI, 2.19-2.95). Violence-exposed and substance use profiles also had significantly higher proportions of women with a detected intraepithelial lesion despite reduced screening participation. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of pregnant women, distinct social vulnerability profiles were differentially associated with cervical cancer screening inadequacy; women with migration-related barriers experienced the greatest disadvantage, and violence-exposed women showed both reduced screening and elevated disease burden. These findings suggest profile-specific interventions could help reduce cervical cancer screening inequalities among socially vulnerable populations.

item.title: Storage and Disposal of Unused Prescription Opioids for Acute Pain After Emergency Department Discharge
item.dc:creator: Raoul Daoust
David Williamson
Vérilibe Huard
Jeffrey J. Perry
Justin W. Yan
Eddy Lang
Alexis Cournoyer
item.description:
Authors: Raoul Daoust, David Williamson, Vérilibe Huard, Jeffrey J. Perry, Justin W. Yan, Eddy Lang, Alexis Cournoyer, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639607
Abstract: Importance Opioid misuse is a major public health concern, and unused prescription opioids can contribute to this problem. Objective To estimate the proportion of unused opioids among patients discharged from the emergency department (ED) for acute pain, evaluate opioid storage and disposal practices, and identify factors that may motivate patients to return unused opioids. Design, Setting, and Participants This cohort study, which was a preplanned substudy of a Canadian multicenter prospective cohort study (Quantity of Opioids for Acute Pain and Limit Unused Medication Group [OPUM] study, with recruitment beginning in May 2019 and follow-up ending in January 2024), included consecutive patients aged 18 years or older discharged from the EDs of 7 hospitals in Québec and Ontario with an opioid prescription for an acute pain condition. Participants were followed up at 2 weeks and 3 months. Exposure Opioid prescription for acute pain at ED discharge. Main Outcomes and Measures The main outcomes were the proportion of participants with unused opioids at 2 weeks and 3 months after ED discharge, opioid storage practices at 2 weeks, and opioid disposal practices at 3 months. Results Of 2590 enrolled participants in the cohort, 2047 (79.0%) completed the 2-week follow-up and 1835 (70.8%) completed the 3-month follow-up. Among participants who completed the 3-month follow-up, mean (SD) age was 51.3 (15.4) years, 947 (51.6%) were male, and mean pain intensity score at triage was 7.1 (2.3) out of 10. At 2 weeks, 1521 of 1811 participants (84.0%; 95% CI, 82.2%-85.6%) reported unused opioids; 102 of 1525 (6.7%; 95% CI, 5.5%-8.1%) stored their opioids in a locked area and 393 of 1525 (25.8%; 95% CI, 23.6%-28.0%) out of reach of children or teenagers. At 3 months, 926 of 1495 (61.9%; 95% CI, 59.4%-64.4%) reported unused opioids, kept mostly for possible future pain (534 [57.7%; 95% CI, 54.4%-60.9%]) or because participants forgot or lacked time to return them (262 [28.3%; 95% CI, 25.4%-31.3%]). Only 614 of 1835 participants (33.5%; 95% CI, 31.3%-35.7%) indicated they would voluntarily return opioids to the pharmacy if prompted, while 479 (26.1%; 95% CI, 24.1%-28.2%) would not return them regardless of incentive offered. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study, 3 months after their ED visit, many participants kept unused prescription opioids at home under suboptimal storage conditions; only one-third were willing to return their opioids to a pharmacy, while more than one-fourth were not. These findings support tailoring opioid prescriptions to individual patient needs to reduce unused medication, alongside strengthening take-back networks and enhancing patient education on safe use, storage, and disposal of opioids.

item.title: Androgen Synthesis Inhibitors vs Androgen Receptor Inhibitors and Survival in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
item.dc:creator: Georges Gebrael
Yeonjung Jo
Varun Nandakumar
Zeynep Irem Ozay
Chiara Mercinelli
Gabriel Hooper
Micah Ostrowski
Nicolas Sayegh
item.description:
Authors: Georges Gebrael, Yeonjung Jo, Varun Nandakumar, Zeynep Irem Ozay, Chiara Mercinelli, Gabriel Hooper, Micah Ostrowski, Nicolas Sayegh, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639458
Abstract: Importance In metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC), randomized clinical trials directly comparing androgen deprivation therapy intensification using androgen synthesis inhibitors (ASIs) vs next-generation androgen receptor inhibitors (ARIs) are lacking. Objective To compare the outcomes associated with ASI vs ARI intensification therapy among patients with mHSPC in community or academic clinical practices. Design, Setting, and Participants This was a retrospective cohort study of patients diagnosed with mHSPC between February 4, 2013, and April 29, 2024, with follow-up through the July 2024 data cut, providing a median (IQR) follow-up of 25.6 (24.5-26.6) months. Patient-level data were extracted from the nationwide US-based Flatiron Health electronic health record–derived deidentified research database of community and academic practices. Patients with evidence of an mHSPC diagnosis initiating treatment with an ASI (abiraterone acetate) or ARI (apalutamide or enzalutamide) within 3 months prior to or 6 months after an mHSPC diagnosis were eligible. Patients with prior docetaxel receipt were excluded. Exposure Treatment with an ASI vs an ARI. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was overall survival (OS), defined as time in months from mHSPC diagnosis to death or censoring at last recorded activity. Results Of 3404 patients (median [IQR] age, 73 [66-80] years), 1830 received treatment with an ASI (abiraterone), and 1574 with an ARI (507 apalutamide, 1067 enzalutamide). Following inverse probability of treatment weighting, patients receiving an ARI had significantly longer OS (median, 67.9 months [95% CI, 67.5 months to not reached]) compared with patients treated with the ASI (median, 57.2 months [95% CI, 52.7-63.3 months]) (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74 [95% CI, 0.64-0.87]); P &amp;lt; .001). Results were similar in sensitivity analyses using therapy initiation as the index date (HR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.62-0.84]; P &amp;lt; .001) and when restricted to index dates on or after December 16, 2019 (HR, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.56-0.81]; P &amp;lt; .001). The association was not modified by insurance status or socioeconomic status. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of 3404 patients with mHSPC, treatment intensification with an ARI was associated with significantly longer OS compared with an ASI. These findings may help guide clinical treatment selection and patient counseling. However, given conflicting clinical practice data across differing database populations, only a randomized clinical trial can definitively answer this question.

item.title: Clinical Evidence on Psilocybin and Its Representation in Media Reporting
item.dc:creator: Kim Madden
Breanne Flood
Imad Kashir
Rayan Ahmad
Hiba Ali
Rotem Petranker
James MacKillop
Anthony Adili
item.description:
Authors: Kim Madden, Breanne Flood, Imad Kashir, Rayan Ahmad, Hiba Ali, Rotem Petranker, James MacKillop, Anthony Adili
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2638843
Abstract: Importance Psilocybin has received increased attention as a potential therapeutic intervention, but it is unclear whether news media reporting reflects the strengths and limitations of the clinical trial evidence. Objective To describe the annual counts of published clinical trials of therapeutic psilocybin and contemporaneous media articles and compare tone, efficacy, and safety messaging. Evidence Review This systematic review included English-language randomized and nonrandomized trials of psilocybin for clinical indications published from January 1, 2014, to October 10, 2024, and media articles describing its clinical use published from January 1, 2014, to April 22, 2025. Trials were found by searching Medline, Embase, PsycInfo, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) and were characterized by design, indication, use of psychotherapy, and reporting of efficacy and safety. Media articles were found through the Factiva database and were characterized by audience, tone, indication, efficacy claim, and safety content. Data were extracted by 2 reviewers. Risk of bias for randomized clinical trials was assessed descriptively using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Findings Annual counts of both published clinical trials (n = 70) and media reports (n = 172) increased from 2018 onward. Depression was the most common clinical indication in trials (47 [67%]) and media articles (138 [80%]), while media articles frequently referenced posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) (74 [43%]) and anxiety (72 [42%]) as clinical indications despite absent and limited trial evidence, respectively, for these conditions. Overall, 49 trials (70%) reported benefit for the primary indication; 125 media articles (73%) made at least 1 positive efficacy claim, and 122 (71%) adopted a favorable tone. Trials typically described small sample sizes of less than 100 participants (65 trials [93%]) and methodologic limitations. Overall, 31 trials (44%) reported safety outcomes, with some (24 [34%]) documenting short-term adverse events, such as transient anxiety, nausea, or headache; long-term safety was rarely assessed (4 trials [6%]). Only 51 media articles (30%) mentioned safety; when harms were discussed, potential long-term psychological risks were sometimes noted (12 articles [7%]). Conclusions and Relevance In this systematic review of clinical trials and media articles, both reported positive effects of therapeutic psilocybin with similar frequency. Academic publications were more cautious and explicit about methodologic limitations, whereas media reports often presented benefits as established, extrapolated them to indications with little or no trial evidence, and provided less safety information. Clarifying these differences in emphasis may support more transparent public communication of indication-specific evidence and uncertainty as interest in psilocybin-assisted treatments grows.

item.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Perioperative Enfortumab Vedotin and Pembrolizumab for Bladder Cancer
item.dc:creator: Zhuo Tony Su
Tyler S. Garman
Carlos A. Rivera Lopez
Ruchika Talwar
Raju Chelluri
Burles A. Johnson
Hiten D. Patel
Akshay Sood
item.description:
Authors: Zhuo Tony Su, Tyler S. Garman, Carlos A. Rivera Lopez, Ruchika Talwar, Raju Chelluri, Burles A. Johnson, Hiten D. Patel, Akshay Sood, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2640370
Abstract: Importance Although cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy for patients with localized muscle-invasive blader cancer (MIBC) is associated with improved survival, nearly half of these patients are ineligible for cisplatin-based chemotherapy and historically proceed to radical cystectomy (RC) without neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Perioperative enfortumab vedotin (EV) plus pembrolizumab with RC is an alternative option, but little is known about its cost-effectiveness compared with surgery alone. Objective To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab for cisplatin-ineligible patients with localized MIBC. Design, Setting, and Participants This economic evaluation developed a decision-analytic Markov model that compared neoadjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab followed by RC and adjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab (intervention arm) vs RC alone (control arm). The sample consisted of simulated patients with MIBC who were ineligible for or declined cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The model was informed by efficacy and safety data from the KEYNOTE-905/EV-303 trial, which had a median (range) follow-up of 25.6 (11.8-53.7) months. Analyses were performed between October 2025 and August 2026. Intervention The 2 treatment strategies were (1) neoadjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab followed by RC and adjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab and (2) RC alone. Main Outcomes and Measures Outcomes included life-years, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and direct medical costs estimated from a Medicare payer perspective over a 10-year horizon. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) was assessed against a willingness-to-pay threshold of $100 000 per QALY. Scenario, 1-way, and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted. Results The model consisted of 10 000 patients (age at baseline, 73 years; 77 900 males [77.9%]). Over 10 years, adding perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab to treatment was associated with increased projected survival from 4.12 to 5.63 life-years per patient, quality-adjusted survival from 3.20 to 4.51 QALYs per patient, and total costs from $317 513 to $412 160. Higher upfront perioperative therapy costs were partially offset by lower postprogression treatment costs ($12 578 per patient for the intervention arm vs $238 729 per patient for the control arm). Perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab with RC achieved an ICER of $72 460 per QALY vs RC alone and therefore represented a cost-effective treatment approach. In 1-way and scenario sensitivity analyses, the cost-effectiveness result was sensitive to alternative assumptions for key factors, including time horizon length, adjuvant therapy utilization rates, patient age, postprogression treatment mix, drug costs, and health utility before disease progression. In the probabilistic sensitivity analysis, perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab with RC had a 53% probability of being cost-effective vs RC alone at the prespecified willingness-to-pay threshold of $100 000 per QALY. Conclusions and Relevance In this economic evaluation of a simulated cohort of patients with cisplatin-ineligible MIBC, clinical trial–informed modeling suggested that adopting the perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab intervention extends overall survival and quality-adjusted survival and is likely cost-effective in the US.

item.title: Skin Toxic Effects and Survival With Enfortumab Vedotin–Pembrolizumab in Advanced Urothelial Carcinoma
item.dc:creator: Zachariah Thomas
Cindy Y. Jiang
Patrick J. Speck
Emanuele Crupi
Mohammad Jad Moussa
Adrienne Joseph
Carly Stender
Michael Glover
item.description:
Authors: Zachariah Thomas, Cindy Y. Jiang, Patrick J. Speck, Emanuele Crupi, Mohammad Jad Moussa, Adrienne Joseph, Carly Stender, Michael Glover, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639517
Abstract: Importance Skin toxic effects are a common early adverse event of enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab (EVP) therapy, but its association with clinical outcomes in patients receiving first-line therapy remains uncertain. Objective To evaluate the association between treatment-emergent skin toxic effects and clinical outcomes among patients receiving first-line EVP. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cohort study was performed at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center among adults with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma receiving first-line EVP therapy between March 3, 2022, and July 31, 2025. Skin toxic effects were used as a time-dependent exposure in Cox proportional hazards regression to account for immortal-time bias. Prespecified sequential adjustment models and 30-day landmark analyses were performed to assess the robustness of the findings. Exposure Treatment-emergent skin toxic effects (rash or pruritus) were identified from medical records. Main Outcomes and Measures Primary outcome was overall survival (OS). Secondary outcomes included progression-free survival and objective response rate (ORR). OS and PFS were measured from EVP therapy initiation to the respective event or last follow-up. ORR was evaluated among patients with a response assessment after the 30-day landmark, according to skin toxic effects status within the first 30 days. Results Among 185 patients (median age, 73 [IQR, 67-79] years; 140 [75.7%] male), skin toxic effects occurred in 98 (53.0%) at a median of 14 (IQR, 7-28) days after EVP therapy initiation. Skin toxic effects of grade 3 or higher occurred in 10 patients (5.4%). Skin toxic effects resulted in EV dose reduction in 31 patients (16.8%), treatment interruption in 20 (10.8%), and treatment discontinuation in 9 (4.9%). At a median follow-up of 17.7 (IQR, 11.3-24.2) months, Simon-Makuch curves demonstrated longer OS and PFS among all patients and longer OS among patients with visceral metastases in the skin toxic effects stratum than in the no toxicity stratum. In adjusted time-dependent Cox proportional hazards regression, skin toxic effects were associated with longer OS (hazard ratio, 0.34 [95% CI, 0.20-0.57]). The association remained consistent across sequential adjustment models and prespecified 30-day landmark analyses. In the 30-day landmark analyses, associations with PFS and ORR remained directionally favorable but were attenuated after multivariable adjustment. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of 185 patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma receiving first-line EVP therapy, treatment-emergent skin toxic effects were associated with longer OS. These findings support further prospective validation of skin toxic effects as an early clinical marker of treatment benefit and investigation of the biological mechanisms underlying this association.

item.title: A Conversation Tool to Enhance Care for People With Type 2 Diabetes
item.dc:creator: Kasia J. Lipska
Megan E. Branda
Anne W. Camp
Melissa Montosa
Rozalina G. McCoy
Victor V. Montori
Felipe Larios
Victor M. Montori
item.description:
Authors: Kasia J. Lipska, Megan E. Branda, Anne W. Camp, Melissa Montosa, Rozalina G. McCoy, Victor V. Montori, Felipe Larios, Victor M. Montori
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639032
Abstract: Importance Effective interventions are needed to support the cocreation of diabetes care plans that are sensible, desirable, and feasible for the people living with diabetes (ie, care that fits). Objective To investigate whether an agenda-setting kit (ASK) added to usual primary care improves fit of care and glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D). Design, Setting, and Participants This single-center, clinician-level cluster randomized clinical trial was conducted from February 16, 2023, to July 26, 2024, with a 6-month follow-up, at a federally qualified health center in New Haven, Connecticut. Eligible clinicians were primary care physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants who prescribed medication to treat patients with T2D. Eligible patients were English- or Spanish-speaking adults aged 18 years or older with T2D and hemoglobin (Hb) A 1c level greater than 8%. Patients were excluded if their clinician determined that an HbA 1c level 8% or lower was inconsistent with goals of care. Data were analyzed from November 7, 2024, to August 13, 2026. Intervention Clinicians were randomized 1:1 to the ASK plus usual primary care group (intervention group) or usual primary care only (control group). The ASK intervention consisted of 14 conversation cards about life with diabetes and its treatment. Prior to the clinical encounter, patients were asked to select 0 to 3 cards they wanted to prioritize for discussion. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was the 6-month change from baseline in illness intrusiveness measured with the Illness Intrusiveness Ratings Scale (IIRS; range: 13-91, with higher scores indicating greater intrusiveness) and HbA 1c level. Secondary outcomes included changes in treatment burden measured with the Treatment Burden Questionnaire (TBQ; range: 0-150, with higher scores indicating greater burden), diabetes distress measured with the 17-Item Diabetes Distress Scale (DDS-17; scores: indicate little or no distress [&amp;lt;2.0], moderate distress [2.0-2.9], and high distress [≥3.0]), and visit satisfaction. Results Eleven clinicians (6 [54.5%] female) were included in the trial along with 143 of their patients. The mean (SD) patient age was 56 (12) years; 87 participants (60.8%) were female and 88 (61.5%) reported Spanish as their primary language. Six-month survey data were available for 65 of 74 patients (87.8%) in the intervention group and 58 of 69 (84.0%) in the control group; data on HbA 1c level were available for 71 (95.9%) and 65 (94.2%), respectively. At 6 months, mean (SD) IIRS scores were 32.1 (15.1) and 37.1 (18.7) in the intervention and control groups (adjusted mean difference, −3.9; 95% CI, −10.4 to 2.6). The mean (SD) HbA 1c levels were 8.8% (1.8) in the intervention group and 9.1% (1.8) in the control group (adjusted mean difference, −0.2%; 95% CI, −0.9% to 0.5%). Mean (SD) TBQ scores in the intervention and control groups were 41.2 (44.8) and 46.8 (44.4) (adjusted mean difference, 1.0; 95% CI, −16.6 to 18.6), and mean (SD) DDS-17 scores were 2.0 (1.0) and 2.3 (1.0) (adjusted mean difference, −0.1; 95% CI, −0.4 to 0.2). Clinician-reported satisfaction was greater in the intervention group; patient satisfaction did not differ between groups. Conclusions and Relevance In this cluster randomized clinical trial of adults with T2D, use of the ASK with usual primary care was associated with greater clinician satisfaction but not with improvements in patients’ fit of care or glycemic control over 6 months. Larger studies should evaluate interventions that not only identify patients’ priorities and treatment burdens but also better support clinicians in addressing them. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05553912

item.title: Concentrated Exposure Therapy vs Internet-Based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
item.dc:creator: Lena Jelinek
Lara Wille
Jakob Scheunemann
Luisa Tegtmeier
Holger Zapf
Franziska Miegel
Lea Schuurmans
Josephine Schultz
item.description:
Authors: Lena Jelinek, Lara Wille, Jakob Scheunemann, Luisa Tegtmeier, Holger Zapf, Franziska Miegel, Lea Schuurmans, Josephine Schultz, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639281
Abstract: Importance Given the high prevalence, chronicity, and associated disability of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), optimizing treatment is a global priority. The Bergen 4-day treatment (B4DT), a concentrated exposure-based intervention, may reduce treatment burden and improve access to evidence-based care. Objective To evaluate the efficacy of B4DT compared with internet-based cognitive behavioral therapy (iCBT) in reducing OCD symptom severity. Design, Setting, and Participants Single-center randomized controlled trial (1:1 allocation). Between May 8, 2024, and August 8, 2025, adults (aged 18 to 72 years) with OCD were enrolled and were followed up for 3 months. Key exclusion criteria included schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, acute suicidality, substance dependence, and recent psychopharmacological changes. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, 6 weeks, 8 weeks (posttreatment), and 3 months (follow-up) by masked evaluators. Interventions Patients were randomized to B4DT (including preparatory sessions) or an 8-week unguided iCBT program. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was the change in OCD symptom severity, measured by the Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS). Secondary outcomes included self-reported OCD (OCI-R), dysfunctional cognitions, quality of life, depressive symptoms, experiential avoidance, global functioning, self-esteem, and treatment satisfaction. Results A total of 253 individuals were screened, and 119 were enrolled after 53 were found to be ineligible and 81 declined to participate. Sixty of the 119 randomized participants (mean [SD] age, 33.5 [10.1] years; 79 [66.4%] women) were assigned to B4DT and 59 to iCBT. The primary analysis included all randomized participants (intention-to-treat). B4DT was associated with significantly greater reductions in OCD symptoms (Y-BOCS) than iCBT, with large effects at posttreatment (mean [SE] difference, −7.9 [0.9]; 95% CI, −9.7 to −6.0; Hedges g , −1.6) and sustained effects at 3-month follow-up (mean [SE] difference, −5.6 [1.1]; 95% CI, −7.8 to −3.4; Hedges g , −1.0). Secondary outcomes consistently favored B4DT. Response and remission rates at 3-month follow-up were higher with B4DT (35 of 57 [61.4%] vs 11 of 44 [25.0%] and 24 of 57 [42.1%] vs 6 of 44 [13.6%], respectively). Conclusions and Relevance In this randomized clinical trial of 119 adults with OCD, B4DT was superior to iCBT in reducing OCD symptom severity, with sustained benefits. Its brief, concentrated format may represent a scalable strategy to improve access to effective OCD treatment globally. Trial Registration German Clinical Trials Register: DRKS00034236

item.title: Mortality Among People With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder
item.dc:creator: Lucy Corrigan
Lauren Heywood
Gavin R. Stewart
Elizabeth O’Nions
Henry Shelford
Joshua Stott
Amber John
item.description:
Authors: Lucy Corrigan, Lauren Heywood, Gavin R. Stewart, Elizabeth O’Nions, Henry Shelford, Joshua Stott, Amber John
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639448
Abstract: Importance Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is associated with adverse life outcomes and increased mortality. Clarifying the magnitude of mortality risks using international data and the potential association between medication and mortality is essential to inform clinical care and motivate public health strategies to address mortality. Objectives To examine the association between ADHD and all-cause and cause-specific mortality and to assess whether mortality risk differs according to ADHD medication use. Data Sources A comprehensive search of PubMed, Web of Science, PsycINFO, EMBASE, MEDLINE, and CINAHL was conducted from database inception to July 8, 2025. Study Selection Eligible studies included quantitative research across all age groups reporting all-cause and/or cause-specific mortality in individuals with ADHD, defined via diagnostic criteria, self-identification, trait measures, or ADHD polygenic risk scores. Exclusion criteria were nonoriginal research, qualitative studies, non–peer-reviewed publications, and studies not reporting mortality outcomes. Data Extraction and Synthesis Data extraction was conducted independently by 2 reviewers. Study quality was assessed by 1 reviewer. Summary data were extracted from published reports, and pooled hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using random-effects model meta-analysis. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and cause-specific mortality (suicide, unintentional or intentional injury, and natural causes), measured using HRs with 95% CIs. Results Nineteen studies including 15 920 970 participants (36.1% female) were included. ADHD was associated with increased all-cause mortality (HR, 1.71; 95% CI, 1.31-2.24; P &amp;lt; .001). Significant associations were also observed for suicide (HR, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.21-2.95; P = .005), unintentional or intentional injury (HR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.22-2.00; P &amp;lt; .001), and natural-cause mortality (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.16-1.38; P &amp;lt; .001). ADHD medication use in people with ADHD was associated with reduced all-cause mortality (HR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.64-0.87; P &amp;lt; .001). Substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies. Conclusions and Relevance In this systematic review and meta-analysis of ADHD and mortality, ADHD was associated with increased mortality across multiple causes; and ADHD medication was associated with a decreased all-cause mortality risk, underscoring the importance of timely diagnosis and treatment. However, the heterogeneity observed across studies highlights the need for standardized methods and improved control of confounding factors to better characterize mortality risk among individuals with ADHD.
